prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (policy-focused, non-ideological)

Economy and business
- Maintain fiscal rules to balance the budget by mid-2020s; simplify taxes; keep VAT level; raise personal allowance to £12,500 and higher rate threshold to £50,000 by 2020; cut corporation tax to 17%.
- Reform business rates (more frequent revaluations, possible self-assessment) and review system for the online era.
- Expand trade: replicate existing EU FTAs, lodge UK WTO schedules, create Trade Commissioners, reconvene Board of Trade, introduce a Trade Bill.
- Tighten corporate governance: binding annual votes on executive pay, publish pay ratios, strengthen worker voice on boards, scrutinise buybacks.
- Strengthen pension protection (new Regulator powers, fines, potential criminal offence).
- Update takeover rules (clear bidder intentions, enforce undertakings, pause powers); protect critical infrastructure.
- Raise the National Living Wage as a share of median earnings; act on gig-economy protections after Taylor Review.
- Crack down on tax avoidance/evasion; boost HMRC capability; improve VAT fraud enforcement.
- Industrial strategy: raise R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years (goal 3%); university investment funds; £23bn National Productivity Investment Fund for housing, R&D, infrastructure, skills; create “Future Britain” funds.
- Support key sectors (advanced manufacturing, shipbuilding, life sciences, oil and gas including decommissioning); back SMEs via procurement (33% target), prompt payment enforcement.

Energy, infrastructure and environment
- Independent review to cut energy costs; industrial energy efficiency scheme; diverse mix with offshore wind leadership; support remote-island wind; develop shale gas (new regulator, planning reforms, community benefit fund).
- Major transport investment: HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion; rail capacity and new services; EV ambition (near-zero-emission cars/vans by 2050); cycling and bus improvements.
- Urban quality measures (air quality, trees, litter, road surfaces); 25-Year Environment Plan; animal welfare (licensing reform, mandatory CCTV in slaughterhouses, restrict live exports).

Brexit, union and immigration
- Leave the EU, seek a comprehensive free trade and customs agreement; Great Repeal Bill to convert EU law; common UK frameworks with devolution; parliamentary vote on final deal.
- Create a UK Shared Prosperity Fund to replace EU structural funds.
- Strengthen the Union; more devolution within a common framework; relocate civil service/Channel 4 outside London.
- Reduce net migration to sustainable levels; align visas with industrial strategy; double Immigration Skills Charge; tighten student and family routes while attracting needed skills.
- Reform asylum focus toward resettlement from conflict regions; support councils and community sponsors.

Security, justice and defence
- Meet NATO 2% and increase defence budget by at least 0.5% above inflation annually; invest £178bn in equipment; retain nuclear deterrent; support veterans.
- Merge infrastructure police forces; fold SFO into NCA for economic crime; enhance cyber security; expand counter-terror work.
- Victims’ law; extend Unduly Lenient Sentence Scheme; modernise courts; prison and probation reform; women’s provision; national community sentencing framework.

Public services, health and social care
- NHS: minimum £8bn real-terms rise over five years; invest in buildings/tech; expand workforce training; seven-day services; mental health (10,000 staff, parity reforms); recover costs from non-residents; raise Immigration Health Surcharge; implement Accelerated Access Review.
- Social care: include home value in means test for domiciliary care; £100,000 asset floor; defer care payments until after death; green paper on quality and integration; statutory carer’s leave; means-test Winter Fuel Payments; retain other pensioner benefits; move from Triple to Double Lock for state pension after 2020; link pension age to longevity.

Education, skills and families
- Expand free schools; allow new selective schools with conditions; require university/independent school sponsorship; specialist maths schools; fairer funding (+£4bn by 2022, no school loses cash); replace universal infant lunches with universal free breakfasts; EBacc targets; teacher support and loan forgiveness.
- Technical education: T-levels (fewer, clearer routes), more hours, mandatory placements; institutes of technology; 3m apprenticeships; UCAS-style technical portal; discounted travel; adult retraining and digital skills right.
- Housing: deliver 1.5m homes by 2022; free up land; modern construction; protect Green Belt; government build 160,000 on public land; council housing deals (fixed-term with Right to Buy); CPO reform; leasehold crackdowns; private renter protections; capture land value; homelessness taskforce, Housing First; halve rough sleeping by 2022, end by 2027.

Digital and consumers
- Digital Charter; new data protection law; Data Use and Ethics Commission; right to delete data at 18; online safety duties and levy for internet harms; counter extremist content online.
- Broadband USO by 2020; full-fibre vouchers; 5G rollout (majority coverage by 2027); 95% geographic mobile coverage by 2022; Verify digital ID; geospatial data body to digitise land/planning.
- Strengthen consumer regulators; simplify rail ticketing and create ombudsman; minimum rail service levels during strikes; energy safeguard tariff cap and smart meters; fuel-poor homes to EPC C by 2030; debt “Breathing Space.”
- Democracy: voter ID; overseas votes for life; boundary review to 600 MPs; repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; retain FPTP; limited Lords reform; end Leveson 2 and repeal Section 40.
